summary_rationale: Cyient Limited is a credible, cash-generative engineering R&D franchise undergoing a high-stakes structural transformation. Its core Digital, Engineering & Technology (DET) segment—anchored by multi-decade Tier-1 relationships with Pratt & Whitney, Airbus, and global rail/telecom OEMs—expanded EBIT margins to a 10-quarter high of 14.2% (₹214 Cr Q2 FCF) under CEO Sukamal Banerjee, while Cyient DLM (record ₹2,813.7 Cr order book, 1.6x book-to-bill, plus a Nov 14, 2026 maritime defense MoU with Hindustan Shipyard) and Cyient Semiconductors (+240.8% YoY, validated by a Nov 18–19, 2026 $10M strategic CCPS equity investment from GlobalFoundries at a $510M post-money valuation) provide secular top-line engines. Historically, Cyient has maintained clean receivables (66 debtor days) and strong cash conversion (₹787 Cr CFO and ₹693 Cr FCF in FY26, 118% CFO/EBITDA). However, Cyient remains CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL (PASS_WITH_WATCH) for four reasons: (1) 5-year sales CAGR slowed to 12.0% with ROCE compressing from 22% (FY24) to 12.3% (FY26), trailing ROE at 8.61%, and organic DET constant-currency growth just +0.4% YoY in Q2 FY27; (2) Cyient Semiconductors posted a -₹30 Cr Q2 FY27 EBIT loss amid foundry/memory tightness (FY28 breakeven target) and DLM faces upfront investment margin drag plus a 119-day Cash Conversion Cycle; (3) simultaneous ₹720 Cr buyback and $303M of 2026 M&A drove gross borrowings up 6.4x to ₹2,759 Cr (0.54x equity, above CRISIL's <0.50x medium-term gearing expectation) while Other Liabilities jumped ₹1,590 Cr to ₹3,727 Cr on ₹926.80 Cr of TAO Digital contingent earnouts (~₹3,686 Cr or 0.72x equity in combined obligations), following ₹71.2 Cr of FY26 aborted-M&A expenses and ₹27.8 Cr of tooling goodwill impairment; and (4) continued C-suite turnover (COO Prabhakar Atla exited Sep 28, 2026; CPO Kavita Kurup resigned Nov 17, 2026) raises post-merger integration risk.
